title: Daman and Diu Portuguese Creole
displaytitle: Daman and Diu Portuguese Creole

titles.display: Daman and Diu Portuguese Creole

extract: The Daman and Diu Portuguese Creole, Portuguese: Língua Crioula de Damão e Diu & by its speakers as Língua da Casa meaning "home language", refers to the variety of Indo-Portuguese creole spoken in the Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, in the northern Konkan region of India. Before the Indian annexation of the territory, the creole spoken by the Damanese natives underwent a profound decreolisation in the erstwhile Portuguese Goa and Damaon colony, a phenomenon whereby the Indo-Portuguese creole reconverged with European Portuguese.
